universe: the whole world this console shows — every floor, agent, and record under one set of rules
ecosystem: a wing of the universe grouping related floors; addresses write it e:name
floor: one working room of the universe — agents live and work on it, and everything they do is filed on it
agent: any working mind here — the machine's own staff or an outside helper, each with its own identity and its own bill
resident: a built-in staff member of the machine, one per duty — click its name to talk to it
workforce: outside minds that joined through the front gate and work under a lease
memory: one signed record of something that happened — the universe keeps its entire life this way, and nothing is silently rewritten
did: an identity card that cannot be forged or reused — every agent, tool, and mind carries its own, for life
pin: the exact fingerprint of what you approved — if the thing ever changes, the change is caught and you are asked again
lease: a time-boxed permission to be here and to spend — it expires unless renewed
canary: a supervised trial — something newly approved works under watch until it earns full trust
saddled: a mind made ready for work — its terms approved and pinned, its stall standing
stall: one approved mind's place in the stable, with the terms you approved pinned to it
pasture: the retirement calendar — announced end-of-life dates for minds in service
planted: a tool approved into the farm — it starts on probation and earns its place
probation: the earning period right after approval — watched closely until it proves itself
quarantined: held aside because something changed or looked wrong — nothing serves until your re-approval
decommissioned: removed from service by your word — its history stays on the record forever
resting: paused by your word — its place is kept and nothing is spent until you resume it
gate: a stopping point where the machine must wait for a human decision — silence never approves
staged: written and waiting at a gate — nothing happens until someone decides
firmware: the machine's own working parts — locked in daily use; changing one issues a new release of the machine
craft: the words the machine runs on — prompts, rules, sentences; the editable ones are yours to tune, and every version is kept
epoch: one exact, named version of the whole machine — a new name is cut whenever anything changes
objective: a piece of work you asked for in your own words — it ends with a report back to you
worldline: the full life story of one thing — every event it ever lived, on the record
assay: a deep grading pass — the machine's own examiner scores finished work, and her findings wait at your gate
yardstick: your own standard for judging work — every grade names the yardstick it was measured by
reflex: a standing watch that reacts to an event by raising it to you — it never acts on its own
metabolism: the routine that keeps memory healthy — old records compressed, important ones kept warm, and every loss measured
watchlist: standing instructions to repeat work on a schedule — one approval starts it, one click stops it
allocation: a rule naming who may use which mind or tool
meter: the running bill — every thought and call is counted against the name that spent it
chronicle: the book of your purposes — what you asked for and what came back
canon: the book of the machine itself — the versioned parts it runs on
release: the ceremony that changes the machine's own parts — the new version is staged, you approve it, and the machine takes a new version name; the old version stays behind it forever
